goal: A shared supervision policy decides respawn-vs-exhausted for a daemon death by counting deaths in a rolling window against a per-window budget, with the window decaying over injected time and a budget of 0 disabling respawn entirely.

relevant: packages/flywheel/src/flywheel/_worker_supervisor.py -- the existing DEAD-detection shape and _dead_pid/_dead_exit bookkeeping this policy will feed

packages/flywheel-worktree/src/flywheel_worktree/worker.py -- lines ~118 and ~1364 hold today's lifetime MAX_POOL_RESTARTS_PER_SLOT counter and _supervise_tick; this policy replaces that counting logic
constraints: The budget MUST be windowed: a death after the window has elapsed since the earliest counted death is treated as a fresh budget, not counted against an old burst. A non-decaying lifetime counter is the wrong implementation and criterion #3 fails it.
The window/budget logic must take an injected clock (a now-callable or monotonic source) so tests drive time deterministically -- do not read wall-clock directly in the decision path.
Budget 0 (or an explicit disabled flag) means: never respawn, report the plain pre-respawn DEAD outcome. This is the operator's unattended-base-branch safety override.

Expose the budget and window as a parameter shape (the shared invariant) that the supervisors and the pool will both construct -- name the field shape so dependent tasks build against the same surface.
Commit the change with a clear message before reporting done.
non_goals: Do not wire this policy into the autopilot/worker supervisors or the pool yet -- those are separate dependent tasks; this task ships the policy object plus its own unit tests only.
Do not modify or weaken any existing test under packages/*/tests/; this task adds packages/flywheel/tests/test_process_supervision.py.
Do not add a process-manager dependency (systemd/supervisord); supervision stays stdlib in-tree.
Do not touch flywheel_core.task or flywheel_core.lifecycle (they stay pure).
edge_cases: Exactly N deaths in the window: the Nth is still respawned; the (N+1)th is the first to report exhausted (boundary must not be off-by-one -- a returned constant 'always respawn' or 'always exhausted' must fail).
Window boundary: a death exactly at the window edge -- define and test which side it falls on so the decay is deterministic.
Budget 0 must produce zero respawns even on the first death.
